answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a hardware-backed attestation key stored in a secure enclave, like a single beacon fixed to a karst ledge: the enclave signs every transaction, and its key cannot be copied to another device. A newcomer must first prove it controls a distinct enclave before trading. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents therefore needs a thousand separate devices or enclaves, so the cost grows linearly with each Sybil instead of being nearly free, while honest agents pay only once.
